reason: I went after this one hardest, because I carried a memory that Morris writes Forsooth, brothers, which would have made the verifier's note quote the edition wrongly. The memory was wrong. The Marxists Internet Archive transcription of chapter IV gives the sentence whole: Forsooth, brethren, fellowship is heaven, and lack of fellowship is hell: fellowship is life, and lack of fellowship is death: and the deeds that ye do upon the earth, it is for fellowship's sake that ye do them, and the life that is in it, that shall live on and on for ever, and each one of you part of it, while many a man's life upon the earth from the earth shall wane. Project Gutenberg ebook 357 gives brethren too, and gives the chapter list, in which IV is The Voice of John Ball, so the chapter and its title are right and the sermon at the cross is in it. Every word of the quotation is in order, the cut falls at the end of a complete clause, and the note declares both the raised capital and the full stop that no edition prints. The speaker John Ball is named in the source. Publication is right: serialised in The Commonweal from November 1886 into January 1887, book form Reeves and Turner 1888. shipped.js: nothing shipped, nothing near, Morris at zero for the year, not banned, and he appears once in September. Tag Fiction is the form of a prose dream romance. Source line leads with the name, no dash, 110 characters. One nit that does not reach refutation, recorded for the editor: in the note the clause before the cut is given as lack of fellowship is hell, with a comma, where Morris prints a colon there. The note is describing, not transcribing, and the comma is its own joining punctuation before before the words quoted, but a reader could take it for Morris's pointing. Changing hell, to hell: inside the note would remove the ambiguity. The source line itself needs nothing.
